skellam

The Skellam distribution is the distribution of the difference of two independent Poisson counts: home goals minus away goals, up-ticks minus down-ticks, spikes in a stimulus window minus spikes in a baseline window. skellam provides its density, distribution function, quantile function and random generation, saddlepoint approximations, maximum likelihood estimation, and a regression model in which both rates depend on covariates.

The distribution functions are accurate to a relative error below 1e-12 for rates up to at least 1e7, and remain finite on the log scale far into the tails, so they can be used safely inside likelihoods. They follow the conventions of R’s own dpois, ppois, qpois and rpois.

Documentation, the changelog and the validation article are on the package website: https://monty-se.github.io/skellam/.

Installation 

install.packages("skellam")              # CRAN
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("monty-se/skellam")   # development version

Usage 

library(skellam)

# X = Y1 - Y2 with Y1 ~ Poisson(12), Y2 ~ Poisson(8)
dskellam(-2:2, 12, 8)                    # P(X = x)
pskellam(0, 12, 8)                       # P(X <= 0)
qskellam(c(0.025, 0.975), 12, 8)         # central 95% interval
set.seed(1)
rskellam(5, 12, 8)                       # random draws (integers)

# Log scale stays finite where the probability itself underflows
dskellam(500, 3, 2, log = TRUE)
pskellam(-1000, 3, 2, log.p = TRUE)

# Large rates
pskellam(0, 1e6, 1e6)

Estimation 

set.seed(1)
x <- rpois(2000, 12) - rpois(2000, 8)
skellam.mle(x)$param                     # close to (12, 8)

Regression

For y = Y1 - Y2, both rates follow a log-linear model in the covariates. param1 describes the rate of the counts that are added and param2 the rate of the counts that are subtracted.

set.seed(123)
n <- 1000
covariate <- rnorm(n)
y <- rpois(n, exp(1 + 0.5 * covariate)) - rpois(n, exp(-0.5 + 0.3 * covariate))
fit <- skellam.reg(y, covariate)
fit$param1                               # intercept ~ 1,    slope ~ 0.5
fit$param2                               # intercept ~ -0.5, slope ~ 0.3

Note for users of version 0.2.4 or earlier: in those versions skellam.reg() returned the two parameter blocks the wrong way round (param1 estimated the rate of the subtracted counts). Results obtained with them should be re-run. See NEWS for all changes.

Background

If \(Y_1 \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_1)\) and \(Y_2 \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_2)\) are independent, \(X = Y_1 - Y_2\) has probability mass function

\[ P(X = x) = e^{-(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)} \left(\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}\right)^{x/2} I_{|x|}\left(2\sqrt{\lambda_1\lambda_2}\right), \qquad x \in \mathbb{Z}, \]

where \(I_\nu\) is the modified Bessel function of the first kind, with mean \(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2\) and variance \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2\). The help page ?skellam describes the numerical methods; the vignette vignette("validate_skellam", package = "skellam") checks every function against the definition.

References

  • Skellam, J. G. (1946). The frequency distribution of the difference between two Poisson variates belonging to different populations. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A, 109(3), 296.
  • Johnson, N. L. (1959). On an extension of the connection between Poisson and χ² distributions. Biometrika, 46, 352–362.
  • Karlis, D., & Ntzoufras, I. (2009). Bayesian modelling of football outcomes: using the Skellam’s distribution for the goal difference. IMA Journal of Management Mathematics, 20(2), 133–145.

Authors

Jerry W. Lewis, Patrick E. Brown and Michail Tsagris wrote the original package. Montasser Ghachem (maintainer) and Oguz Ersan made the corrections and extensions from version 0.2.5 on. Please report bugs at https://github.com/monty-se/skellam/issues, and cite the package with citation("skellam").
